## Themes

These rows serve two capabilities. model-council gains a branch that turns independent candidates into one artifact, scored against criteria, picked and grafted, and delegation keeps model choice and dispatch. A new skill, interrogate, sends adversaries to break a change or design and keeps only a finding a run proves.

Suggested: delegation · purpose match: model-council · flag: suggested differs
Purpose: Upstream runs several candidates at one task, picks a base and grafts the best of the rest into one artifact. Ours runs independent members and a judge to reach an answer; a branch that turns candidates into one artifact belongs there, since it keeps the judge and the isolation.
Reason: Compared with model-council: the only unit of ours with independent members and a judge, as playbook-map §3 row 17 records. Suggested delegation by the computed signals only.

Purpose: Upstream sends adversaries to break a change or design and keeps only findings a run proves. Ours has no unit for this until interrogate is built; review judges by reading and reports every finding.
Reason: Compared with none: interrogate, the row target, does not exist yet, and --with takes only an existing skill. Suggested review by the computed signals only.

### Blind extraction

1. adversarial-break-mandate: Assign adversaries to attempt to break a change or design rather than to assess it in general. (SKILL.md:9)
2. run-proof-survival-gate: Let a finding stand only when an executed run demonstrates it. (SKILL.md:9)
3. report-only-no-fixes: Limit the result to reporting findings, with no fixes applied. (SKILL.md:9)
4. user-named-scope: Use the scope the user names when one is given. (SKILL.md:13)
5. default-branch-diff-scope: Without a named scope, cover the branch's diff from its merge base with the base branch up to and including the working tree. (SKILL.md:13)
6. intent-restatement: Restate the change's intent in the agent's own words before fanning out. (SKILL.md:13)
7. intent-evidence-sources: Derive that intent from the user's message, the commits and the pull request description. (SKILL.md:13)
8. ask-when-intent-unclear: Ask the user when the intent cannot be established. (SKILL.md:13)
9. reviewer-list-from-configuration: Choose adversary models from a dedicated reviewer line in the user-level model configuration rule, using the sibling skill's runner-selection and fallback steps. (SKILL.md:17)
10. isolated-adversary-worktrees: Give each adversary its own output location through the sibling skill's worktree-first step. (SKILL.md:17)
11. same-message-background-adversaries: Launch all adversaries in one message as background subagents through the sibling skill's fan-out step. (SKILL.md:17)
12. adversary-dropout-tolerance: Continue when an adversary produces nothing and record the dropout, through the sibling skill's fan-out step. (SKILL.md:17)
13. uncommitted-changes-seeded: Copy the scope's uncommitted changes into each adversary's worktree. (SKILL.md:17)
14. general-purpose-adversary-type: Spawn each adversary as the general-purpose subagent type. (SKILL.md:17)
15. adversary-brief-contents: Give each adversary the scope, the intent and one fixed brief in place of a task and rationale request. (SKILL.md:17)
16. proof-against-real-code: Require each finding to be shown by a run against the actual code, such as a failing test, a reproduction script or revealing command output. (SKILL.md:19)
17. design-review-by-prototype-or-probe: For a design or plan, prove findings by running a prototype or probing the current tree. (SKILL.md:19)
18. repros-confined-to-own-worktree: Keep reproduction material inside the adversary's own worktree. (SKILL.md:19)
19. finding-report-template: Require each finding to carry a title, the exact command, the printed output and the output the intent demands. (SKILL.md:19)
20. exclude-unrun-claims: Omit anything the adversary did not actually run. (SKILL.md:19)
21. exclude-style-and-speculative-risk: Exclude style, naming, structure and hazards that only matter after a future change. (SKILL.md:19)
22. empty-result-permitted: Accept a report with no findings as a legitimate outcome. (SKILL.md:19)
23. coordinator-reruns-commands: Have the coordinator verify each finding by executing its command again. (SKILL.md:23)
24. two-part-keep-test: Retain a finding only if the output shows the failure and that failure violates the intent. (SKILL.md:23)
25. drop-unverified-findings: Remove every finding that fails the keep test. (SKILL.md:23)
26. root-cause-merge: Combine findings that share one root cause. (SKILL.md:23)
27. no-judge-pick-or-graft: Omit cross-judging, base selection and grafting from this flow. (SKILL.md:25)
28. union-of-verified-findings: Keep all verified findings across adversaries rather than selecting one adversary's list. (SKILL.md:25)
29. output-intent-section: Open the output with the intent restatement. (SKILL.md:29)
30. output-finding-fields: For each verified finding, report its command, its output and how it violates the intent. (SKILL.md:30)
31. adversary-attribution: Name the adversaries that found each verified finding. (SKILL.md:30)
32. explicit-no-findings-statement: State explicitly that there are no verified findings when none remain. (SKILL.md:30)
33. dropped-finding-accounting: Report per adversary how many findings were dropped and why. (SKILL.md:31)
